entry.title: BitCraft Online
entry.content:
Our color palette follows the harmony rule of split complementary colors which uses two colors across the color wheel, with those two colors lying on either side of the complementary color. For each primary color, we have subtle shifts in tone that provide a level of flexibility and utility for creating subtle patterns and segmentation of information.
The default color palette for Bitcraft with a high contrast, dark on light palette. The alternative color palette for BitCraft with a dark background color enabling a more comfortable gaming experience in low-light situations.
A type ramp establishes a range of font sizes, styles, and weights used for different elements within a composition. It helps create a visual hierarchy and guides readers through the content by emphasizing important information and structuring the text. The augmented 4th, 1.414, is a proportion that works well for more content dense interfaces that strike balance between complex information and breathability. A font size of 14 pixels ensures that the text is legible for most users without appearing too small. It provides comfortable reading for an average viewing distance of around 20-24 inches from the screen.
Our art deco-inspired shape language grounds itself in highly geometric shapes. Our iconography maintains a consistent look and feel through the use of a combination of vertical, horizontal, and diagonal lines that intersect each other at 45 or 30 degree angles.
Spacing is used to create visual proximity between related information, grouping those elements together.
A core part of our shape language includes stroke dividers and patterns that frame content. These strokes should only be used in only two weights: 4px and 8px.

Role

  • Defined the visual identity and UI systems for BitCraft, establishing the game’s look and feel across menus, HUDs, and player interfaces.
  • Created a pipeline connecting game design, visual design, and engineering, improving communication and reducing implementation friction across disciplines.
  • Developed a Notion-based documentation and handoff process to track features, specs, and component ownership, enabling smoother iteration and clearer collaboration.
  • Created templates for the marketing team to generate consistent and high-quality YouTube, Steam, and social media assets.

entry.summary: I designed and animated the logo reveal for SpacetimeDB, a distributed database technology project by Clockwork Labs. Using Blender and After Effects, I created a visual narrative inspired by gravitational lensing, light bending around a black hole, culminating in the reveal of the logo. The animation established a cinematic yet scientific tone that reflected the brand’s focus on scale, depth, and innovation.

Silent Hill Ascension
entry.summary: I was a UI/UX Designer on Silent Hill Ascension, a new form of interactive entertainment developed by Genvid that blended television with gaming. The experience allowed viewers to participate in live storylines by playing minigames to earn points, which were then used to vote on key narrative decisions. Votes were tallied weekly, with the story progressing based on community input. My role was to design the user experience and interface systems that supported this hybrid format, ensuring gameplay, voting, and storytelling were intuitive and engaging for a global audience.

entry.title: Room Renders

entry.title: Stream Pirates
entry.content:
Captain.tv was a startup company creating games designed for streamers and their viewers with the goal of enabling collaborative, community-building gaming experiences. Not seeking to compete with the likes of main stream games, Stream Pirates was the second game following the major success of Stream Raiders, to act as a side game that a streamer would run regularly throughout their stream. I was brought on as the sole UX and UI designer for this the game. As the Senior Visual Designer at Captain.tv, I was responsible for shaping the UI/UX of Stream Pirates during its development phase. Working closely with the art team, I explored multiple visual and interaction directions, created the full UI system, and implemented every screen, component, and transition directly in Unity. My work aligned a diverse set of visual influences—pixel art gameplay, painted key art, and streamer-friendly readability—into a unified experience.

Problem

The game’s early development included multiple competing visual styles and evolving gameplay systems, making it difficult to establish a cohesive brand and UI direction. The challenge was to create an interface that felt native to the pixel-art world while still supporting the broader illustration-based marketing identity. The UI also needed to scale across streamer overlays, gameplay views, and interactive elements used by both players and viewers.

Design Process

I conducted a broad exploration of visual styles—color, typography, component shapes, and HUD paradigms—before narrowing into a hybrid direction that blended pixel-art textures with clean painted accents inspired by the key art. This created a visual bridge between game and brand. I then built a full UI system in Unity, including reusable prefabs, responsive layouts, iconography, and in-game feedback patterns tailored to fast, chaotic, streamer-centric gameplay. Close collaboration with the key-art illustrator ensured consistency across promotional materials, in-game visuals, and Twitch presentation.

Outcome & Impact

I established a unified visual direction that bridged pixel art and illustrated key art, delivered a complete UI system implemented in Unity, and enabled the team to iterate quickly with a scalable, production-ready interface. The work strengthened the game’s identity during early development and streamlined collaboration across design, art, and engineering.
